html:
"Welsh" is the map's label, for 800 and 900, for the Welsh, the Britons of Wales, who lived in several small kingdoms such as Gwynedd, Powys, Dyfed and Gwent.

After the end of Roman rule the Britons of the west kept their Brittonic language and their Christian faith while the Anglo-Saxons took the east. The Welsh called themselves Cymry, "fellow countrymen". In the late 700s King Offa of Mercia built a long earthwork, Offa's Dyke, along the border.

In the 800s Rhodri the Great of Gwynedd joined much of Wales under one rule and fought off Viking raids. His grandson Hywel Dda is remembered for the Welsh laws. The Welsh kings often had to accept the overlordship of Wessex and its English successors, and to the south lay their cousins in Dumnonia.
